incubate.definition: v. grow under conditions that promote development
incubate.translation:
vt. 孵, 培养, 使发展
vi. 孵蛋, 潜伏, 筑巢, 孵化, 酝酿
n. 孵育物

incubated.translation: v. （卵）被孵化( incubate的过去式和过去分词 ); 孵（卵）; <医>潜伏; 逐渐形成

incubates.definition:
v grow under conditions that promote development
v sit on (eggs)
incubates.translation: v. （卵）被孵化( incubate的第三人称单数 ); 孵（卵）; <医>潜伏; 逐渐形成

incubating.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Incubate
incubating.translation: v. （卵）被孵化( incubate的现在分词 ); 孵（卵）; <医>潜伏; 逐渐形成

incubation.definition:
n. maintaining something at the most favorable temperature for its development
n. (pathology) the phase in the development of an infection between the time a pathogen enters the body and the time the first symptoms appear
incubation.translation:
n. 抱蛋, 孵化, 酝酿
[医] 孵育, 孵化, 潜伏, 宿庙求梦(古希腊)

incubations.definition:
plural of incubation
n. maintaining something at the most favorable temperature for its development
n. (pathology) the phase in the development of an infection between the time a pathogen enters the body and the time the first symptoms appear
incubations.translation:
(incubation 的复数) n. 抱蛋, 孵化, 酝酿
[医] 孵育, 孵化, 潜伏, 宿庙求梦(古希腊)

incubative.definition:
a. Of or pertaining to incubation, or to the period of
   incubation.
incubative.translation: a. 孵蛋的, 潜伏的

incubator.definition: n. apparatus consisting of a box designed to maintain a constant temperature by the use of a thermostat; used for chicks or premature infants
incubator.translation:
n. 孵卵器, 细菌培养器, 早产儿保育器
[化] 恒温箱; 孵化箱

incubatorium.translation: 育囊, 单孔类动物胸部的孵袋

incubators.definition: n. apparatus consisting of a box designed to maintain a constant temperature by the use of a thermostat; used for chicks or premature infants
incubators.translation: n. 孵化器( incubator的复数形式 ); （用于放置早产婴儿的）恒温箱

incubi.translation: n. 梦淫妖( incubus的名词复数 ); 噩梦; 像噩梦压迫着人的事物; 精神压力

incubous.definition:
a. Having the leaves so placed that the upper part of each
   one covers the base of the leaf next above it, as in hepatic mosses of
   the genus Frullania. See Succubous.

incubus.definition:
n. a male demon believed to lie on sleeping persons and to have sexual intercourse with sleeping women
n. someone who depresses or worries others
incubus.translation:
n. 梦淫妖, 梦魇, 沉重的负担
[医] 梦魔, 梦魇

incubuses.translation: n. 梦淫妖( incubus的名词复数 ); 噩梦; 像噩梦压迫着人的事物; 精神压力

incudes.definition: n the ossicle between the malleus and the stapes

incudiform.translation: [医] 砧形的, 铁砧形的

inculcate.definition: v. teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions
inculcate.translation: vt. 反复灌输, 谆谆教诲

inculcated.translation: v. 极力主张, 反复灌输( inculcate的过去式和过去分词 )

inculcates.definition: v teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions
inculcates.translation: v. 极力主张, 反复灌输( inculcate的第三人称单数 )

inculcating.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Inculcate
inculcating.translation: v. 极力主张, 反复灌输( inculcate的现在分词 )

inculcation.definition: n. teaching or impressing upon the mind by frequent instruction or repetition
inculcation.translation: n. 反复灌输, 谆谆教诲

inculpable.definition: s free of guilt; not subject to blame
inculpable.translation: a. 不能陷害的, 无辜的, 无可非议的

inculpate.definition: v suggest that someone is guilty
inculpate.translation:
vt. 使负罪, 控告, 使连累
[法] 控告, 连累, 归罪于

inculpated.translation: v. 显示（某人）有罪, 使负罪( inculpate的过去式和过去分词 )

inculpates.definition: v suggest that someone is guilty
inculpates.translation: vt. 显示（某人）有罪, 使负罪（inculpate的第三人称单数形式）

inculpating.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Inculpate
inculpating.translation: v. 显示（某人）有罪, 使负罪( inculpate的现在分词 )

inculpation.definition: n an accusation that you are responsible for some lapse or misdeed
inculpation.translation:
n. 归罪, 连累, 责难
[法] 控告, 归罪, 连累

inculpative.definition: a causing blame to be imputed to

inculpatory.definition: a. causing blame to be imputed to
inculpatory.translation:
a. 使人负罪的, 责难的
[法] 可指控的, 可归罪的, 连累的

incult.definition: a. Untilled; uncultivated; crude; rude; uncivilized.
incult.translation: a. 未开垦的, 未耕种的, 无教养的

inculture.definition: n. Want or neglect of cultivation or culture.
inculture.translation: 没教养, 没文化, 不开化

incumbencies.translation: n. 现任职位, 现任职权, 任期( incumbency的名词复数 )

incumbency.definition:
n. a duty that is incumbent upon you
n. the office of an incumbent
incumbency.translation:
n. 任职, 义务, 任职期
[法] 职责, 义务, 在职

incumbent.definition:
n. the official who holds an office
s. lying or leaning on something else
s. necessary (for someone) as a duty or responsibility; morally binding
s. currently holding an office
incumbent.translation:
a. 现任的, 依靠的, 负有义务的
n. 领圣俸者, 在职者

incumbently.definition: adv. In an incumbent manner; so as to be incumbent.

incumbents.definition: n. the official who holds an office
incumbents.translation: n. 教区牧师( incumbent的复数形式 ); 教会中的任职者

incumbered.translation: v. 妨害, 阻碍( incumber的过去式和过去分词 )

incumbering.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Incumber
incumbering.translation: v. 妨害, 阻碍( incumber的现在分词 )

incumbers.translation: 妨害, 阻碍（incumber的第三人称单数形式）

incumbrance.definition:
n a charge against property (as a lien or mortgage)
n an onerous or difficult concern
n any obstruction that impedes or is burdensome

incumbrancer.definition:
n. One who holds an incumbrance, or some legal claim,
   lien, or charge on an estate.
incumbrancer.translation: [法] 对土地有其他物权者

incumbrances.definition:
plural of incumbrance
n a charge against property (as a lien or mortgage)
n an onerous or difficult concern
n any obstruction that impedes or is burdensome
incumbrances.translation: (incumbrance 的复数) n.阻碍物, 累赘

incunables.translation: (incunable 的复数) n.古书之一册

incunabula.translation: 摇篮期, (在欧洲指1500年以前印的)古版本

incunabular.translation: a. 初期的,摇篮时期的,古艺术品的

incunabulist.translation: n. 古刊本鉴定家, 精通初期刊本知识的专家

incunabulum.definition:
n. A work of art or of human industry, of an early epoch;
   especially, a book printed before a. d. 1500.
incunabulum.translation:
n. 最初期, 古版书
[医] 出生地点

incur.definition: v. make oneself subject to; bring upon oneself; become liable to
incur.translation:
vt. 招致, 蒙受, 遭遇
[经] 招致, 蒙受, 担负

incurability.definition:
n. incapability of being cured or healed
n. incapability of being altered in disposition or habits
incurability.translation: n. 不能医治, 不能矫正

incurable.definition:
n. a person whose disease is incurable
a. incapable of being cured
s. unalterable in disposition or habits
incurable.translation:
a. 不能医治的, 不能矫正的, 无救的
n. 不治的病人, 无救的人

incurableness.definition: n. The state of being incurable; incurability.
incurableness.translation: n. 无法治愈, 不可救药

incurables.definition:
plural of incurable
n. a person whose disease is incurable
a. incapable of being cured
s. unalterable in disposition or habits
incurables.translation:
(incurable 的复数) a. 不能医治的, 不能矫正的, 无救的
n. 不治的病人, 无救的人

incurably.definition:
r. to an incurable degree
r. in a manner impossible to cure
incurably.translation: adv. 治不好地, 不能矫正地

incure.translation: [法] 招致, 引起, 惹起

incuriosity.definition:
n. Want of curiosity or interest; inattentiveness;
   indifference.
incuriosity.translation: n. 无好奇心, 没趣味

incurious.definition: a. showing absence of intellectual inquisitiveness or natural curiosity
incurious.translation: a. 无好奇心的, 不关心的, 平凡无趣的

incuriously.translation: 无好奇心地; 不关心地

incurred.definition:
v make oneself subject to; bring upon oneself; become liable to
v receive a specified treatment (abstract)
incurred.translation: v. 遭受；招致（incur的过去分词）

incurrence.definition: n. the act of incurring (making yourself subject to something undesirable)

incurrent.definition:
a. Characterized by a current which flows inward; as, the
   incurrent orifice of lamellibranch Mollusca.
incurrent.translation: a. 向内流的, 流入的

incurring.definition: n. acquiring or coming into something (usually undesirable)

incurs.definition:
v make oneself subject to; bring upon oneself; become liable to
v receive a specified treatment (abstract)
incurs.translation: v. 遭受, 招致, 引起( incur的第三人称单数 )

incursion.definition:
n. the act of entering some territory or domain (often in large numbers)
n. the mistake of incurring liability or blame
incursion.translation: n. 侵入, 侵略, 奇袭

incursions.definition:
plural of incursion
n. the act of entering some territory or domain (often in large numbers)
n. the mistake of incurring liability or blame
incursions.translation: (incursion 的复数) n. 侵入, 侵略, 奇袭

incursive.definition: s. involving invasion or aggressive attack
incursive.translation: a. 流入的, 侵入的

incurvate.definition:
v. bend inwards
v. cause to curve inward
s. bent into or having an inward curve
incurvate.translation:
v. (使)向内弯曲
a. 向内弯曲的

incurvated.translation: v. （使）向内弯曲, （使）弯曲( incurvate的过去式和过去分词 )

incurvates.definition:
v bend inwards
v cause to curve inward
incurvates.translation: v. （使）向内弯曲, （使）弯曲（incurvate的第三人称单数形式）

incurvating.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Incurvate
incurvating.translation: v. （使）向内弯曲, （使）弯曲( incurvate的现在分词 )

incurvation.definition: n. the action of creating a curved shape
incurvation.translation:
n. 内曲
[医] 内曲, 弯曲

incurvature.definition: n a shape that curves or bends inward

incurve.definition: v. t. To bend; to curve; to make crooked.
incurve.translation:
n. 内曲, 内曲线球
vt. 使内曲

incurved.definition: s bent into or having an inward curve
incurved.translation: a. 弯曲的, 内弯的

incurving.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Incurve
incurving.translation:
n. 内弯；内曲线球
vt. 使…向内弯曲
vi. 向内弯曲（等于incurvate）

incurvity.definition:
n. A state of being bent or curved; incurvation; a bending
   inwards.
incurvity.translation: n. 内弯；内曲线球 (incurve的变形)

incus.definition: n. the ossicle between the malleus and the stapes

incuse.definition:
v. t. Cut or stamped in, or hollowed out by engraving.
v. t. Alt. of Incuss
incuse.translation:
a. 铸印的
n. 铸印图案
vt. 铸印于硬币上

incuss.definition:
v. t. To form, or mold, by striking or stamping, as a coin or
   medal.
incuss.translation: n. 【解剖学】砧骨 [参较 malleus, stapes]
